item.text: I’m reviewing the current split so the next refactor is still meaningful. At this point the useful work is in reducing duplicated responsibilities between the demo, the facade, and the algorithm layer rather than touching the sort behavior again.

I’m taking this pass toward sharing the range abstraction across the facade and the engine. Right now `QuickSort` validates raw bounds and `QuickSortAlgorithm` has its own private range type, so I’m collapsing that into one package-private type with validation built in.
The shared range refactor is in. I’m compiling the updated source set and then re-running the demo cases so the new common range type is verified in both the public API path and the algorithm path.
The refactor compiles. I’m running the same representative inputs again so the shared `IndexRange` path is exercised through the facade and the algorithm.

The next refactor is in [IndexRange.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/010_quick_sort/IndexRange.java:1), [QuickSort.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/010_quick_sort/QuickSort.java:1), and [QuickSortAlgorithm.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/010_quick_sort/QuickSortAlgorithm.java:1).

I pulled the half-open range concept into a shared `IndexRange` type. That moves bound validation and `length()` logic out of `QuickSort`, removes the algorithm’s private duplicate range type, and gives both the public facade and the internal engine one consistent representation for slice semantics. `QuickSort` is now smaller again, and `QuickSortAlgorithm` no longer owns validation-adjacent plumbing.

Verification: `javac QuickSort.java QuickSortAlgorithm.java QuickSortDemo.java IndexRange.java` succeeded. `java QuickSortDemo` prints `[1, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10]`, `java QuickSortDemo 4 2 9 2 -1` prints `[-1, 2, 2, 4, 9]`, and `java QuickSortDemo 5 1 5 3 5 2 5` prints `[1, 2, 3, 5, 5, 5, 5]`.
